steps.title: You need to be able to convert between all three number bases
steps.body: decimal (base 10), binary (base 2), and hexadecimal (base 16). There are six possible conversions to master.

steps.title: Method
steps.body: Write out the binary place values above each bit. Add up all the place values where there is a 1. Ignore positions with a 0.

steps.title: Method
steps.body: Repeatedly divide the decimal number by 2. Record the remainder each time (it will always be 0 or 1). Read the remainders from bottom to top to get the binary number.

steps.title: Method
steps.body: Find the largest power of 2 that fits into the number. Subtract it and put a 1 in that position. Repeat with the remainder. Put 0s in positions where the power doesn't fit.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Convert binary 11001010 to decimal. | Convert decimal 200 to binary (8 bits). | Convert hex A5 to decimal.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Write out the place values above each binary digit - it prevents mistakes For binary-to-hex, group from the RIGHT in groups of 4 For hex-to-binary, always write 4 bits per hex digit (pad with zeros) Division remainders are read BOTTOM to TOP Practise all six conversions until they become automatic In the exam, show your working - you can get partial marks
